payload.stem: A solid sphere rolls without slipping from rest down an incline from a height of $0.5\text{ m}$ and reaches the bottom with a speed of $2.65\text{ m/s}$. A second solid sphere with $3$ times the mass and $2$ times the radius rolls without slipping from rest down the same incline from a height $4$ times as great. What is the best prediction of the speed of the second sphere at the bottom?

options.why: Scales the speed with the height factor to the first power.

For a solid sphere $mgh=\tfrac12mv^2+\tfrac12\left(\tfrac25mR^2\right)\omega^2$ gives $v=\sqrt{10gh/7}$, which does not depend on the mass or the radius, so $v\propto\sqrt{h}$: $2.65\text{ m/s}\times\sqrt{4}=5.29\text{ m/s}$.
Includes the factor for the mass, as if a heavier sphere rolls faster.
Leaves the speed unchanged because the mass and radius changed.
